subject: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol 🧠, OpenAI Agent Plugins Standard 🔌, Block Buzz Work
intro: OpenAI is having quite a week. GPT-5 turns one tomorrow, and they're celebrating by shipping on two fronts at once. The pattern is clear: OpenAI is moving from model releases to platform control . Smarter models and the standard everyone must build on. Agent Plugins with Google, Amazon, Microsoft onboard is not a feature, it's a land grab for the agentic layer. The real question we're watching: who actually owns the ecosystem when the standard is "open"?

news.headline: OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT with GPT-5.6 Sol, cutting factual errors by 68%
news.body: OpenAI just reshuffled what every ChatGPT plan actually runs under the hood. Here is what changed and why it matters. GPT-5.6 Sol now powers all paid chat modes for Plus and Pro users, both quick replies and deep reasoning, as one unified experience. No more switching between modes manually. The accuracy jump is real. 68% fewer factual errors compared to GPT-5.5 Instant, tested across finance, medicine, and law prompts. The model now pushes back when agreeing with you would actually be wrong. Plus and Pro users also get a new reasoning effort slider , so you control how much thinking goes into each response. Fast answer or deep analysis, your call. Free users are not left out. GPT-5.6 Luna becomes the new default with unlimited text chats, plus a Think button that gives Luna extra time on harder questions.
bullets: Plus/Pro: updated Sol + reasoning slider, live now
Free/Go: Luna as default, unlimited text, Think button rolling out
Codex and Work: unchanged, separate Sol version

news.headline: OpenAI launches Agent Plugins open standard to share tools across Codex, Cursor, Copilot
news.body: Until now, building an AI agent plugin meant rebuilding it separately for every tool. Different manifest formats, different folder layouts, different configs. You'd end up maintaining multiple copies of the same thing, watching them slowly drift apart. Agent Plugins 1.0.0 fixes that. It's an open, vendor-neutral standard for packaging your agent skills and MCP servers (think: connectors that let AI agents talk to external tools) into one portable format that works everywhere. At launch, your plugin works across: The format is dead simple. A directory, a plugin.json with a name, and your skills folder. That's a valid plugin. Components fail independently, so one broken MCP server won't take down your whole plugin. The steering committee includes Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI, Vercel, and now Google. Build once, ship everywhere.
bullets: ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, VS Code, and Kiro
Google is now joining as a core maintainer too

news.headline: Jack Dorsey open-sources a free self-hosted workspace with built-in AI agents
news.body: Jack Dorsey's company Block just open-sourced Buzz , a self-hosted workspace where you and AI agents share the same rooms. Think Slack plus GitHub plus automation, but running on your own server. No subscriptions. No vendor lock-in. 22.8k stars already. Here is what makes it different. Agents are not bots bolted on the side. They join channels, review code, run workflows, and orchestrate other agents, with their own identity and audit trail. Same permissions model as a human teammate. What you can actually do with it: To get started: git clone, run just dev , and your relay is live at localhost:3000. Built in Rust, Apache 2.0 licensed.
bullets: Host chat, search, Git events, and YAML-based automation in one place, all on your own server
Add AI agents (Claude, Codex, Goose) to any channel and scope exactly what each one can touch
Turn a feature branch into a room where patches, CI results, and review all live together
Query six months of project history in plain English and get answers with receipts
